basics.name: Kirill Kondratiuk
basics.label: Software Engineer
basics.summary: Backend Software Engineer with 4+ years of experience designing, developing, and delivering scalable, fault-tolerant systems. Skilled at guiding complex projects from initial architecture through performance optimization and long-term maintainability in production. Brings a strong Computer Science foundation, ICPC problem-solving experience, and a track record of mentoring peers, influencing technical decisions, and delivering high-quality, efficient solutions built to last.

work.name: Talon.One
work.summary: Incentives engine for enterprise promotions and loyalty.

work.name: freiheit.com technologies
highlights: Played a key role in the end-to-end delivery of a mission-critical, multi-country system — from architecture design to production launch — including on-site deployments in pilot countries and remote rollouts with ongoing support to 30+ others. Contributed to substantial performance improvements, with the platform running 3× faster overall and certain workflows accelerated by up to 10× (15 minutes down to 1.5 minutes), all while maintaining or enhancing data consistency and security.

Designed and implemented a resilient event-streaming pipeline from the legacy system’s database to the new platform’s event stream, enabling cross-team data access without breaking the domain ownership model. Reduced critical data retrieval times from 30–60 minutes to 30 seconds, significantly speeding up dependent workflows across multiple teams.

work.name: HawkEye (local)
highlights: Implemented a fully functional Android app that can simultaneously track and record a football match using object prediction and tracking.
Latency was around 300ms — enough to track most amateur-league matches.

work.name: Brightwave
highlights: Delivered core frontend functionality using a previously created RESTful API.
Optimized main-page loading so there was no waiting time after start by buffering the most probable next content for a user.

work.name: Yandex
highlights: Optimized interaction between two highly loaded services by implementing a new compression mechanism, saving 2.4% CPU and 5% network resources.
Added integration and unit tests for the new code; coverage increased from 80% to 94%.
Gradual launch into production with zero downtime.
